problem_statement.value: I need to keep a standard 96-well microplate of diagnostic reagents between 2 and 8 C for 72 hours during land shipment across a hot climate, with no battery, no electronics, and no ice resupply. Phase-change gel packs make the parcel too heavy to ship economically. What cooling approach could actually work, and how would I know it works before I ship?
